summary.headline: KRBL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 6% to INR1,526 crore as record domestic sales (+22%) offset a 33% export drop from Middle East disruption; PAT INR155 crore.
summary.overview: Domestic revenue hit a record INR1,230 crore in Q4 (+22% YoY) on 16% rice volume growth and 5% realisation growth, while exports fell to INR279 crore (vs INR450 crore) as the Iran/Israel/US conflict and March 2026 shipping disruption hit Middle East shipments. Q4 gross margin fell to 29.6% (from 31.5%) and EBITDA margin to 15.5% (from 16.2%), with PAT of INR155 crore (10.1% margin) against INR154 crore a year earlier. For FY26, total income rose 9% to INR6,168 crore, with EBITDA margin of 15.8% and PAT margin of 10.5%. Management said Q1 export trends are hard to call and gave no monthly export numbers; it expects demand to rebound once the conflict settles.

financial_highlights.change: margin improved on lower input costs and higher other income

financial_highlights.change: vs negative INR405 crore a year earlier

segments.name: Domestic branded rice
segments.commentary: Q4 domestic revenue INR1,230 crore (+22% YoY) on 16% volume and 5% realisation growth; FY26 domestic revenue excl. power INR4,444 crore (+10%), with branded basmati +9% and branded volume +8%.

segments.name: Branded non-basmati
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR78 crore (+44% YoY from INR54 crore); FY26 INR271 crore (+38% from INR197 crore).

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR279 crore (-33% YoY) on lower Middle East shipments; FY26 INR1,555 crore (+6%). Q4 basmati export realisation about INR1,38,500–1,39,000 per MT.

segments.name: Edible oil (Uplife)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR12 crore; early stage, general trade distribution being built, with management guiding to healthy double-digit growth in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Domestic: management is targeting about 10% organisation-level volume growth in FY27, and expects a further 2–3% improvement in average domestic realisation in Q1 FY27 versus about INR79,000–80,000 per MT in Q4.

Exports: no numeric guidance; management said April ran in line with Q4 trajectory, while May and June were still unclear. It expects exports to rebound sharply once the Middle East conflict settles, and said the recent lost volumes could be recovered in three to four months after settlement.
Inventory: 530,000 tonnes of rice-equivalent stock at 31 Mar 2026. Management expects to build inventory in the coming season, depending on crop and pricing, and sees the export demand as strong.
Edible oil: expects healthy double-digit growth in FY27.
Real estate: Samalkha (Panipat) land parcel of about 130 acres; the 60-acre portion is earmarked for own warehousing near Sonipat/Barota, and no monetisation decision has been taken.
capex_capacity: Inventory at 31 Mar 2026: total INR3,714 crore, including paddy INR879 crore (230,000 tonnes) and rice INR2,667 crore (427,000 tonnes), versus INR2,934 crore rice at 31 Mar 2025 (476,000 tonnes).
Rice-equivalent inventory of about 530,000 tonnes against FY26 sales of about 560,000 MT domestic and 160,000 MT export.
Distribution: 3.4 lakh retail outlets, 16 C&F agents and 8 super stockists; supply chain shift towards an FOR model.
Samalkha land parcel (about 130 acres, split by GT road): the 60-acre side is for KRBL's own warehousing given space constraints at the Barota plant.
demand_pricing: Domestic branded basmati: Q4 realisation about INR79,000–80,000 per MT; price stabilisation and brand investment supported growth, while Q3 domestic revenue was flat YoY on competitive and pricing pressure.

Market share in packaged basmati (FY26): general trade 36.9%, modern trade 38.7%, e-commerce 40.1%. Management said Q4 share was 100–200 bps higher than the full-year level in each channel; it did not give a YoY comparison for Q4.

Exports: Middle East shipments were hit in March 2026. Cargo has largely reached destinations since April–May. Alternate routes (Khor Fakkan, Jeddah, Salalah, Jordan for Iraq) carry higher freight, insurance and transit times. Management reports Saudi business is continuing.

Industry: India's FY26 basmati exports rose about 8% to 6.5 million MT (record); non-basmati exports about 15 million MT (+6%). Pakistan Super Basmati has traded at a premium to Indian 1121 since October 2025 (USD1,180–1,220/MT FOB).
Global: USDA sees 2026-27 global rice production at about 538 million MT versus 543 million MT, with consumption rising to about 541 million MT. Management said this could keep prices firm.

qa_highlights.question: Export run-rate: how much further decline versus Q4 in Q1, and April numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no April or monthly export figures and said Q1 depends on the geopolitical situation. Ashish said April was 'in the same trajectory' as Q4, with May and June still to be seen.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory build-up for FY27 and the competitive environment in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Anoop Gupta said inventory will be built in the coming season, depending on crop and pricing. Management cited a 8–9% margin on unsold stock and about 35–40 tonnes of export rice at Kandla (about 20% cheaper than current prices), which could be sold domestically.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic volume growth and whether Q4 can be sustained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets about 10% organisation-level domestic volume growth in FY27; Q4 volume growth was 16%.

qa_highlights.question: Use of about INR1,000 crore cash: special dividend or buyback?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashish said only the approved INR103 crore dividend (450%) was in scope; no other capital return measures were announced.

qa_highlights.question: Real estate: why not monetise the Samalkha land and what about the buyback question?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60-acre portion will be used for own warehousing despite the higher profit from a sale. It is evaluating opportunities but will only invest in real estate if the return could double the investment.

qa_highlights.question: Basmati price outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to comment, as the India Rice Exporters' Association crop-size contract is still being mapped; a view on FY27 pricing awaits the crop size.

qa_highlights.question: Saudi distributor appointment and channel inventory in exports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is staying selective and direct with wholesalers in Saudi Arabia; no distributor has been appointed. Ashish declined to quantify channel inventory but said most Middle East markets are below normal stock levels.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and Strait of Hormuz disruption: export volumes, freight and war-risk insurance cost, and timing of restocking demand.
Export volumes in Q1 FY27 with no April or monthly data given; management declined to share run-rate figures.
Gross margin compression (29.6% in Q4 vs 31.5%) from higher COGS and lower other income; freight costs have not been quantified.
Pending ED matter (sub judice): management would not take questions on it.
Real estate capital allocation: the Samalkha land parcel and about INR1,000 crore of cash, with no clear return-deployment plan.
Domestic competitive intensity and channel share, with Q4 share gains not quantified and the FY share trend showing a decline per the analyst's reading.
Monsoon and crop outcome for 2026 (possible deficient monsoon) and the basmati price trajectory.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the domestic business and the medium-term export rebound, but cautious and evasive on near-term exports, April–June numbers, FY27 pricing and real estate, deferring to the geopolitical outcome and crop size.
key_quotes: Quarter 4 financial year 2026 was our best ever quarter for domestic revenue.
So once the war is settled, I think the exports will double up in next six months because there has been a big gap as far as food reserves are concerned.
Now Saudi orders are coming. We are there in the market.
So we intend to develop our own business. That is in mind as far as real estate is concerned.

growth.why: Management targets ~10% domestic volume growth in FY27 and a further 2-3% realisation gain in Q1 FY27, backed by market share gains and price stabilisation but no specific capacity additions; export outlook is unquantified, with April in line with Q4 and May-June unclear.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 15.5% from 16.2% and gross margin to 29.6% from 31.5%, but domestic realisation is guided up a further 2-3% in Q1 FY27 from INR79,000-80,000 per MT, and FY26 EBITDA margin was 15.8%; freight and war-risk costs are unquantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity commissioning was discussed; the Samalkha 60-acre parcel is for own warehousing (storage, not production) and rice-equivalent inventory of about 530,000 tonnes is being held rather than capacity added.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management is working towards about 10% organisation-level domestic volume growth in FY27 after Q4 domestic volume grew 16%, backed by market share at 36.9% general trade, 38.7% modern trade and 40.1% e-commerce.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Net cash of INR789 crore and about INR1,000 crore of cash on hand with no stated return-deployment plan; management only approved the INR103 crore dividend and said it will invest in real estate only if returns could double the investment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Exports could rebound sharply once the Middle East conflict settles, with lost volumes recoverable in 3-4 months after settlement, but April was only 'in the same trajectory' as Q4 and May-June are unclear.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Export revenue fell 33% YoY to INR279 crore in Q4 (from INR450 crore), with Q1 export run-rate undisclosed and freight, insurance and transit costs on alternate routes rising.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product launch was discussed; branded non-basmati grew 44% to INR78 crore in Q4 but no new launch was named.

rows.label: Middle East export rebound after conflict settles
rows.why: Exports fell to INR279 crore in Q4 (vs INR450 crore) and management says lost volumes could be recovered in three to four months after settlement, but no settlement date is set.

rows.label: Inventory build for FY27 season
rows.why: Stock is 530,000 tonnes rice-equivalent against FY26 sales of about 720,000 MT (560,000 domestic plus 160,000 export), and management will build inventory depending on crop and pricing; an 8-9% margin on unsold stock is cited.

rows.label: Domestic realisation step-up in Q1 FY27
rows.why: Management guided a further 2-3% improvement in average domestic realisation from about INR79,000-80,000 per MT in Q4, with price stabilisation supporting it.

tone.note: Management was confident on domestic volume (Q4 +16%) and the medium-term export rebound, but cautious and evasive on April-June exports, FY27 basmati pricing, and the use of about INR1,000 crore cash and Samalkha land; analysts pressed on export run-rate, capital allocation, and FY27 pricing.
